Project console / Stage A / Single VPS

A Supabase-compatible backend you run on one VPS.

Lumo Base deploys the official Supabase self-hosted stack as a single-host Compose project. Every image is pinned to upstream tag self-hosted/v0.8.4; every port, key and repo path below is verified against that tag. Stage A covers phases 0–9.

Open quickstart → Read the compatibility contract

Free for all internal use. Billing and monetization are deliberately deferred to a later phase; this console documents no commercial control plane.

03 / Request path

Client to Postgres

All external traffic enters through Caddy on 443, crosses the Envoy gateway, and terminates in one of the application services before reaching Postgres. No service is addressed directly from the public interface.

client --HTTPS :443--> Caddy --:8000/tcp--> api-gw (Envoy) api-gw --> auth :9999 | rest | storage :5000 | meta :8080 | studio :3000 auth / rest / storage --> db :5432 (pooled: supavisor :6543 --> db)

Ports shown are the verified internal bindings. rest has no internal port recorded in the upstream inventory and is represented here by name only.

Request path hops
#HopComponentDetail
01ingressCaddydeploy/proxy/Caddyfile. Terminates TLS on 443 and forwards to the gateway's internal API_GW_HTTP_PORT=8000.
02gatewayapi-gw (Envoy)envoyproxy/envoy:v1.39.6. Routes auth, rest, storage, meta and studio. Dashboard access is guarded by DASHBOARD_USERNAME / DASHBOARD_PASSWORD HTTP basic auth.
03servicesGoTrue / PostgREST / StorageInternal bindings: auth 9999, storage 5000, meta 8080, studio 3000. PostgREST port: —.
04dataPostgresPOSTGRES_PORT 5432, optionally through supavisor on 6543. Never published externally.
04 / Network & ports

Public versus private

Only 443 is exposed publicly. Every other binding is internal to the host and reachable through the gateway or from inside the Compose network.

Studio is not published directly. It is reached through the gateway and protected by DASHBOARD_USERNAME / DASHBOARD_PASSWORD HTTP basic auth. PROXY_DOMAIN is the proxy host setting; no endpoint URL is reproduced here.

06 / Security baseline

RLS, GRANTs and key separation

Three independent controls. A request that clears the gateway still has to clear the database policy layer, and no client-facing credential is ever promoted to server authority.

Row Level Security

Tables reachable through PGRST_DB_SCHEMAS require RLS enabled with policies checked into database/policies/. tests/security/ asserts that a client-shaped request cannot read rows outside its grant.

database/policies/ · tests/security/

Explicit GRANTs

Privileges are granted explicitly in database/migrations/; there are no blanket grants to client-facing roles. PGRST_DB_MAX_ROWS bounds result size and PGRST_DB_EXTRA_SEARCH_PATH bounds schema resolution.

PGRST_DB_MAX_ROWS · PGRST_DB_EXTRA_SEARCH_PATH · PGRST_DB_SCHEMAS

JWT vs API-key separation

Token verification material is configured through JWT_SECRET, JWT_KEYS, JWT_JWKS, ANON_KEY_ASYMMETRIC and SERVICE_ROLE_KEY_ASYMMETRIC; JWT_EXPIRY bounds token lifetime. Publishable and anon keys authenticate clients; SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY and SERVICE_ROLE_KEY stay server-side and are never forwarded by the proxy or gateway.

The permitted redirect surface is defined by SUPABASE_PUBLIC_URL, API_EXTERNAL_URL, SITE_URL and ADDITIONAL_REDIRECT_URLS. Signup behaviour is controlled by DISABLE_SIGNUP, ENABLE_EMAIL_SIGNUP and ENABLE_EMAIL_AUTOCONFIRM.

Verified configuration surface

# Database POSTGRES_HOST POSTGRES_DB POSTGRES_PORT POSTGRES_PASSWORD # Auth and key material JWT_SECRET JWT_EXPIRY JWT_KEYS JWT_JWKS ANON_KEY SERVICE_ROLE_KEY ANON_KEY_ASYMMETRIC SERVICE_ROLE_KEY_ASYMMETRIC SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY DISABLE_SIGNUP ENABLE_EMAIL_SIGNUP ENABLE_EMAIL_AUTOCONFIRM # Public URL and redirects SUPABASE_PUBLIC_URL API_EXTERNAL_URL SITE_URL ADDITIONAL_REDIRECT_URLS # Dashboard and secrets DASHBOARD_USERNAME DASHBOARD_PASSWORD SECRET_KEY_BASE VAULT_ENC_KEY PG_META_CRYPTO_KEY # Gateway, proxy and compose API_GW_HTTP_PORT PROXY_DOMAIN COMPOSE_FILE # Storage GLOBAL_S3_BUCKET REGION STORAGE_TENANT_ID # PostgREST PGRST_DB_SCHEMAS PGRST_DB_MAX_ROWS PGRST_DB_EXTRA_SEARCH_PATH # Pooler POOLER_TENANT_ID POOLER_DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE POOLER_MAX_CLIENT_CONN

07 / Compatibility contract

What the SDK can rely on

Every compatibility claim is an assertion that must be backed by a real supabase-js integration test. Without a passing test in tests/integration/, a capability stays in the Not implemented class.

Compatibility classes, definitions and required evidence
ClassDefinitionRequired evidence
Fully compatible Core auth, REST data access and storage operations served by enabled Stage A services through the gateway. Passing supabase-js integration tests in tests/integration/; result recorded in docs/COMPATIBILITY.md.
Partially compatible Behaviour that works on the pinned stack but depends on an optional capability or on a default not enabled on this host. Test plus an explicit note of the limiting condition in docs/COMPATIBILITY.md.
Not implemented Capabilities whose services are Deferred in the inventory, plus anything outside Stage A scope. Listed as Deferred in docs/VERSIONS.md and docs/ROADMAP.md; no compatibility claim is made.

Not implemented in Stage A: realtime subscriptions (supabase/realtime:v2.148.3), edge functions (supabase/edge-runtime:v1.77.9), image transforms (darthsim/imgproxy:v4.0.21) and deno-cache.

08 / Operations & backup

Restore drills, not backup files

A backup counts only after a restore drill rebuilds a working stack on a clean host. Tooling lives in ops/backup/; host and service signals are configured in ops/monitoring/.

Restore drill sequence

  1. Snapshot the POSTGRES_DB database and store the artifact off-host.
  2. Stop the stack defined in deploy/compose/ via COMPOSE_FILE.
  3. Restore onto a clean host using keys declared in deploy/env/.env.example.
  4. Reapply database/migrations/ and database/policies/.
  5. Run tests/security/ and tests/integration/ against the restored stack.
  6. Confirm 443 is the only published port and the gateway answers on API_GW_HTTP_PORT=8000.

Run drills against the constrained target (2 vCPU / 4 GB RAM / 40 GB SSD) so restore timing reflects the real host. Recommended headroom is 4 CPU / 8 GB RAM / 80 GB SSD. There is no Kubernetes, MinIO or multi-node failover path in Stage A.
